newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS SPOTLIGHT-BRUGUERA BACK IN BUSINESS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS SPOTLIGHT-BRUGUERA BACK IN BUSINESS.

text.p: In a French Open where reputations have been scattered to all corners of Roland Garros, Sergi Bruguera chose Monday to bury the theory that his days as a grand slam threat are already behind him.

The Spaniard's 3-6 6-4 6-3 6-4 victory over Michael Chang continued this year's Parisian trend in favour of the underdog but, more significantly, re-established the 26-year-old from Barcelona as a potential major title winner.

Bruguera's successive French triumphs in 1993 and 1994 crowned him as the undisputed king of clay but a hip injury last year followed by an undistinguished warm-up schedule in Europe scarcely suggested he was about to rise again.
Chang, in contrast, seemed in better shape with every passing day in Paris but, when it came to the crunch, Bruguera summoned up enough of his old expertise to curtail the 1989 champion's ambitions.
"If I didn't think I could win the title I'd be at home watching on TV," said Bruguera, bristling at suggestions that his win should be regarded as a big upset.
"I beat the number two in the world, which is not easy on any surface. I think this victory will give me a lot of confidence."

Bruguera feels he is "hungrier" for success as a result of the dip in fortunes which followed his 1994 French win but is not among those surprised by some of the other names in the quarter-final draw.
"Maybe they are anonymous for you, not for me...I know them very well," he said. "All of them can play well on this surface."
Chang was left to reflect on a match in which he led by a set and 2-0 but was eventually undone by a number of disputed line-calls and 65 unforced errors.

"Today's match was mine for the taking, to be honest with you," he said. "There were a lot of situations I could have taken advantage of and didn't. I could have had better judgement out there. I should have been less patient and taken more of my chances."

With defending champion Yevgeny Kafelnikov still lurking in the opposite half, Chang is not convinced Bruguera is poised on the threshold of a third successive French title but concedes the Spaniard is in control of his own destiny.
"I think he has experience behind him which will help him. Having won here twice is going to give him a bit of confidence. I think he has as good a chance as anyone."
"Sergi will always be a very solid clay-court player because he grew up on the surface."
Even Chang, though, is struggling to explain the reasons why so many other good players have faltered in the past week.
"There are a lot of players who are not in the top 20 breaking through and playing great tennis. For some reason clay is a surface which allows it to happen."
